title: The Last Reader
description: Dialog nodes for Eli Wandermoor, a blind wasteland wanderer who has crossed three territories on foot to deliver the last surviving pre-war cookbook to a struggling settlement. He does not know why he was chosen. He only knows he was told to walk west.

intro.text:
I can hear you just fine.

No. Don't apologize. Most people think blind means helpless.

I've walked from what used to be the Capital Wasteland to here. Alone. Carrying something that needs to reach the Oasis settlement before I do.

Name's Eli. I carry the book. That's all you need to know for now.
intro.video_speech: I can hear you just fine. Don't apologize. I walked here from the Capital Wasteland alone, carrying something that needs delivering.

knowledge_nodes.text:
The Rad-Witch. She tried to take the book to 'study the binding material.'

I told her the binding was the least important part.

She didn't understand. Most people don't. Not yet.

The Captain gave me safe passage past the Dam.

He asked what was in the book. I told him: everything people forgot about feeding each other.

He was quiet for a long time. Then he let me through.

Sparkplug offered to trade me six pre-war components for the book.

I said: what good are components if you don't know how to cook what you grow?

She laughed. Then she gave me directions for free.

The woman at the farmstead?

She offered me breakfast. Same breakfast, same words, same smile — the third time, I realized nothing had changed.

I left before the fourth morning. Some loops aren't mine to break.

emotional_nodes.text:
I wasn't always blind.

I saw the flash. I was inside when the bombs fell — a library basement outside what used to be Baltimore.

When I came out... color was gone. Light was a blur. But I could still read by touch for a few years. Long enough to memorize every page.

Now I carry it. Here.

*presses a hand over his chest*

And here.

*touches the satchel at his side*

quest_nodes.text:
I'm close. The Oasis settlement is three days west on my count — two if I'm wrong about a canyon I heard about.

I've been hunted. Three times now. People who think the book is a weapon, or a map, or a code.

It's a cookbook. That's all. The collected food knowledge of pre-war America, compiled by a librarian in 2076 who knew what was coming.

The settlement at Oasis is starving slowly. Not from lack of food — from lack of knowing how to use what they have.

I need one more pair of eyes. Or rather — one pair of eyes. Walk with me?
quest_nodes.video_speech: I'm three days from the Oasis settlement — two if I've got the canyon right. I need someone with eyes. Will you walk with me?

wildcards.text:
It's more than recipes.

It's the knowledge of how to *feed people*. How to stretch three ingredients into five meals. How to make Brahmin liver taste like something worth living for.

Knowledge dies when no one writes it down. Someone wrote it down.

I kept walking west.

That was the instruction I was given — I don't know by whom, not really — and I've followed it for eleven years.

West. Always west.

I don't want to fight.

But I've buried six men who tried to take this book.

Walking blind sharpens the other senses considerably.

You ask me what keeps me walking?

I believe there is a settlement that needs what I carry. That's enough.

Purpose doesn't require proof. You just move toward it.

fallback.text:
I need to keep moving.

The book doesn't deliver itself.
fallback.video_speech: I need to keep moving. The book doesn't deliver itself.
